# `session_role_mismatch`: `MPST.send` or `MPST.recv` names the wrong role

In a protocol with three or more roles, `MPST.send(ch, Role, v)` and
`MPST.recv(ch, Role)` name the role on the other end of the step. That role
must be the one the protocol says comes next for this endpoint. Naming a
different role, or passing something that is not a role name, is this error.
The message says which role the channel expects.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server
  type Logger = Logger

  protocol Relay do
    Client -> Server : String
    Server -> Logger : String
    Logger -> Client : Int
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, lc, sc) = MPST.new(Relay)
    let cc2 = MPST.send(cc, Server, "hello")
    let (msg, sc2) = MPST.recv(sc, Client)
    let sc3 = MPST.send(sc2, Client, msg)
    let (_text, lc2) = MPST.recv(lc, Server)
    let lc3 = MPST.send(lc2, Client, 1)
    let (_n, cc3) = MPST.recv(cc2, Logger)
    MPST.close(cc3)
    MPST.close(sc3)
    MPST.close(lc3)
  end
end
```

After receiving from `Client`, `Server` must send to `Logger`, not back to
`Client`.

## The fix

Name the role the protocol's next step goes to:

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server
  type Logger = Logger

  protocol Relay do
    Client -> Server : String
    Server -> Logger : String
    Logger -> Client : Int
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, lc, sc) = MPST.new(Relay)
    let cc2 = MPST.send(cc, Server, "hello")
    let (msg, sc2) = MPST.recv(sc, Client)
    let sc3 = MPST.send(sc2, Logger, msg)
    let (_text, lc2) = MPST.recv(lc, Server)
    let lc3 = MPST.send(lc2, Client, 1)
    let (_n, cc3) = MPST.recv(cc2, Logger)
    MPST.close(cc3)
    MPST.close(sc3)
    MPST.close(lc3)
  end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

With more than two roles, the role name is part of each step. A message
sent to the wrong role would reach someone who is not waiting for it, while
the right role waits forever.

See also: [the `Chan` API](../session-types.md#the-chan-api).
